exercise.name: Barbell One Leg Hip Thrust
aliases: Barbell B-stance hip thrust (straight free leg)

reference.title: Barbell one leg hip thrust
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in at the bottom, breathe out as the hips drive up, hold briefly at the top, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 0.8 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen and much lighter than a two-leg hip thrust; use a bar pad. Leave about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Heavier bar, then a 2 s squeeze at the top.

cues.text: Lower shoulder blades on the bench edge, bar (with a pad) across the hip crease, hands just outside the hips. Right foot flat under the knee, left leg straight off the floor.
Tuck the chin, brace, drive through the right heel until the hips and trunk are level, shin vertical.
Squeeze the right glute at the top without arching the lower back; keep the pelvis level.
Lower slowly until the plates touch the floor.
Brief reset, then the next rep.

mistakes.mistake: Hips tilting toward the free leg
mistakes.fix: Keep the pelvis level: push the working knee slightly out and brace.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the lower back at the top
mistakes.fix: Tuck the chin and ribs down; finish with the glutes, not the back.
Drive through the heel; set the foot so the shin is vertical at the top.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the bar roll toward the belly
mistakes.fix: Hold the bar on the hip crease with both hands and use a pad.

kinematics.norm: About knee height so the upper back can pivot on the edge (common coaching)
From deep flexion with the plates down to neutral at the top (Contreras 2015)
About 90 degrees at the top, shin vertical (common coaching)
Trunk level with the thighs at the top (common coaching)
Bar across the hip crease, padded (common coaching)
Pause at the top, slow lowering (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell one leg hip thrust, video (movement reference only)

Contreras, Vigotsky, Schoenfeld, Beardsley & Cronin 2015, a comparison of gluteus maximus, biceps femoris and vastus lateralis EMG in the back squat and barbell hip thrust (J Appl Biomech 31(6):452-458)

Selkowitz, Beneck & Powers 2013, which exercises target the gluteal muscles while minimizing activation of the tensor fascia lata? Fine-wire EMG of 11 exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 43(2):54-64)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

cautions: Use a thick bar pad over the hips; roll the bar into place from the floor.
Use a bench that cannot slide (against a wall or loaded).
Keep the chin tucked; do not let the neck arch over the bench.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Hip-bone discomfort: thicker pad, lighter bar.
Pelvis tilting: two-leg barbell hip thrust first.
regressions: Two-leg barbell glute bridge on the floor.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Main hip extensor; hip thrusts drove more upper and lower gluteus maximus activity than back squats (Contreras 2015).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Main hip extensor; hip thrusts drove more upper and lower gluteus maximus activity than back squats (Contreras 2015).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension; less active with the knees bent about 90 degrees at the top.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension; less active with the knees bent about 90 degrees at the top.
muscleNotes.quads_r: Working side holds the knee angle; free side keeps the lifted leg straight.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Working side holds the knee angle; free side keeps the lifted leg straight.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Help extend the hips and keep the knees from flaring.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Help extend the hips and keep the knees from flaring.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on one leg (working side); single-leg bridging raises gluteal demand over the two-leg version (Selkowitz 2013; Boren 2011).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level on one leg (working side); single-leg bridging raises gluteal demand over the two-leg version (Selkowitz 2013; Boren 2011).
muscleNotes.core: Holds the ribs down so the lower back does not arch at the top.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the spine neutral; the movement should come from the hips, not the lower back.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the spine neutral; the movement should come from the hips, not the lower back.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the bar in place on the hips.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the bar in place on the hips.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Help pin the bar to the hips with straight arms.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Help pin the bar to the hips with straight arms.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Press down on the bar to steady it.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Press down on the bar to steady it.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Hold the free leg straight off the floor.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Hold the free leg straight off the floor.
